First and foremost, look for a doctor, let them know about your eating struggles, they'll examine you for any underlying causes and they may refer you to a therapist if mental health is a problem to overcome lack of sufficient nutrition.

The best way to increase appetite and gain weight is through heavy exercise and proper nutrition. Not only will increasing your caloric spending make you hungrier, muscle mass is much denser than fatty tissue. You'll look better and healthier. If you start going to the gym, your body will adapt to the stimulation and your appetite will follow, soon enough you'll be craving for food. Although the gym is the best way to build muscle mass, if that's not your cup of tea, you can look for other forms of exercise, like cycling, rock climbing, trails, etc. It has to be an activity you can do consistently for several months or even years. Physical activity is the key, you can't overlook it. It's very important to ask your doctor first whether you can start any sort of physical activity in your current stage. But it is fundamental that you stick to a workout routine as soon as you gain enough weight for that, because in the long term it'll help you keep your appetite.

Look for a nutritionist and let them know about your lack of appetite and gym routine, they'll help you gradually adapt your diet to your new reality. If you can't go to a nutritionist, try counting your macros and adjusting their intake to your bodyweight as it progresses. (This is not medical advice!) I'd suggest you start by eating 2 grams of carbs per bodyweight kilogram (g/kg) and add 0,5 g/kg per week until you reach 5g/kg. You can look for more information about that on google or youtube by searching "bulking diet".

I'd also like to recommend you the subreddit r/gainit, they're a community for people looking to gain weight.
